gen-dafont-groovy-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Groovy squeezes its c down to a narrow slit and spaces its lowercase loosely, with arms and legs that never change width. Schibsted Grotesk is the opposite, a plain sans with wide-open e and a shapes and tall bowls, so a larger heading would let both show.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sen: Groovy's c nearly seals itself shut, and its loosely tracked lowercase has a funky, friendly bounce to it. Sen sits underneath, tall and open.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sintony: Groovy pinches its c to a thin slit and keeps every arm and leg the same width, which gives it a funky, loose-limbed look. And Sintony, a sans-serif with a chunky tall midzone and no clogged curves, would carry a long page smoothly.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sofia-sans: Funky and tightly shut, Groovy nearly closes its c and keeps arms and legs the same width. But if the heading shrinks, that slit gets lost, while Sofia Sans, a sans-serif with tall, rounded, openly sided letters, holds up fine.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-stack-sans-notch: Loose, funky letters with a nearly closed c: that is Groovy, friendly and a bit cheeky. And it earns its keep big and short, while Stack Sans Notch, a plain sans, lets you see right into every curve.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-stack-sans-text: Groovy pinches its c almost shut and spreads its lowercase out, friendly and funky in every line. But Stack Sans Text, a sans with a marker-like line and well-spaced curve endings, is the one built for steady reading.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sulphur-point: Groovy's c narrows to a slit, its lowercase is loosely tracked, and its arms and legs keep one width, all of it friendly and funky. Sulphur Point, a sans with distinct gaps and bulky lowercase, would read steadily.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-tiktok-sans: TikTok Sans reads open and tall, its x-height rising close to cap height. Groovy answers with funky, loosely tracked letters and a c that nearly closes, so the two feel like a loud friend next to a modern, spacious one.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-ubuntu-sans: Groovy's c almost seals shut. Its loose, funky lowercase is where it shines, while Ubuntu Sans, a sans-serif with big-eyed letters and tubular strokes that stop before closing, handles the quieter work.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-vend-sans: Friendly and a little funky, Groovy nearly closes its c and spaces its lowercase loosely. Yet Vend Sans, a sans-serif drawn with a ruler-straight line and wide, unclosed curve ends, gives the page somewhere to rest.
